ai.summary: An independent evaluation group says Anthropic’s AI development pace has roughly doubled compared with last year, with AI itself likely helping accelerate research. The finding raises questions about whether safety practices can keep pace with faster capability gains.
ai.title: Anthropic is rapidly accelerating AI development amid slowdown calls, outside research group says

ai.summary: Environmental and conservation organizations are using AI for work such as climate analysis and wildlife monitoring, while warning that data centers’ electricity, water use and emissions create significant environmental costs. The trade-offs are expected to feature in discussions around the upcoming COP31 climate conference.
ai.title: Environmental groups embrace AI, even as they warn of data center impacts

ai.summary: Staff at a U.S. government division responsible for assessing AI safety have been asked to report informally to a White House office, according to former officials. The arrangement has prompted concerns about the independence of the division’s research and assessments.
ai.title: Staff at the US center for AI safety are reporting to the White House, raising independence concerns

ai.summary: An investigation reports that U.S. officials approved dozens of Chinese companies to handle Nvidia H200 chips, including some with ties to sanctioned firms. The findings have drawn scrutiny to how the approvals are vetted and how export restrictions are enforced.
ai.title: US cleared dozens of Chinese firms to handle Nvidia chips, some with ties to sanctioned companies

ai.summary: About 600,000 Nvidia H200 AI chips are reportedly in Hong Kong awaiting approval to enter mainland China, despite U.S. authorization for exports. China’s effort to protect its domestic chip industry is complicating access to high-performance processors used by its AI companies.
ai.title: 600,000 Nvidia Chips Stuck in Hong Kong Amid Chinese Rules

ai.summary: China’s Moonshot AI reportedly explored leasing Nvidia Blackwell computing capacity from European data centers, including clusters of thousands of GPUs. The talks highlight how overseas cloud access may complicate export controls that restrict advanced chips from entering China.
ai.title: China’s Moonshot AI sought Nvidia chip access in Europe amid U.S. curbs

quantum.summary: Riverlane announced a method for identifying correlated errors from measurement data. The company reported a 75% reduction in logical-error rates in simulations and a 14% improvement when applied to experimental data from Google’s superconducting processor.
quantum.title: Riverlane Introduces New Quantum Error Correction Method

quantum.summary: IBM and the University of Chicago unveiled an operational Quantum System Two at Hyde Park Labs, powered by IBM’s Nighthawk processor. The system is intended to support research and eventually anchor the National Quantum Algorithm Center.
quantum.title: IBM unveils its first quantum computer in Illinois at Hyde Park Labs

quantum.summary: IBM, Oak Ridge National Laboratory and AMD launched a co-design platform for quantum error-correction research, combining quantum systems with classical computing resources. The collaboration is part of work targeting a scientifically relevant quantum computer by 2028.
quantum.title: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) Launched A Quantum Error Correction Research Platform

quantum.summary: Quantinuum reported a third-quarter loss but raised its full-year revenue outlook and described plans to evolve its Nexus developer platform toward fault-tolerant computing. Its roadmap includes the planned Apollo system, targeted for 2029.
quantum.title: Quantinuum: Q3 Earnings Snapshot

quantum.summary: IQM said it demonstrated a Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger entangled state across all 54 qubits of its Emerald processor. The report says the result was made available to cloud users; the performance claims are from the company.
quantum.title: IQM Quantum Computers Oyj Demonstrates Entanglement Across Complete 54-Qubit Processor

quantum.summary: Physical Superintelligence said a research system produced a proof of the Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture, with the steps formally checked using Lean. The result concerns limits on quantum speedups for certain random-input problems; it is a company-reported claim covered by the outlet.
quantum.title: Stanford Team Confirms At Physical Superintelligence's Proof Of Quantum Speedup Limits
